narrative: Material PL3__MBAA96BA exhibits smooth, high-volume daily demand (~49,811 units/day, CV=0.175) with no statistically significant trend over the observed period (Mar 2025–Mar 2026). Lead times are volatile (mean 1.56 days, CV=0.626), which drives ~95% of total lead-time demand uncertainty and necessitates a meaningful safety stock of 82,040 units. The storage capacity constraint (349,999 units) is binding and caps the order quantity well below the unconstrained EOQ; a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended with ROP=159,831 and Q=267,958, delivering an estimated annual cost saving of ~$7,315 versus the current SAP baseline.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand (CV=0.175) with high and predictable volume is ideally suited to a continuous-review (r,Q) model: trigger a fixed replenishment order Q whenever stock falls to reorder point r. The MOQ of 83,078 is accommodated within the EOQ-derived order quantity. The storage cap is respected by capping Q at floor(max_storage - SS).
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity constraint is fully binding. The order quantity (267,958) plus safety stock (82,040) equals 349,998 units — effectively at the 349,998.93 unit ceiling. Any increase in safety stock requirements (e.g., due to worsening lead time volatility) would require a corresponding reduction in order quantity, increasing ordering frequency and annual ordering costs. If demand grows materially, the capacity will need to be expanded or the MOQ renegotiated.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ(83,078) + SS(82,040) = 165,118 which is below max_storage_units(349,999). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility. Capacity constraint binds on the order quantity, not the minimum order.
